1.explanation:
• packages/react/src/components/Toggle/Toggle.js – add a readOnly prop, apply aria-readonly when readOnly is true (and disabled is false), prevent value changes, and attach a CSS modifier class (e.g. bx--toggle--readonly).
• packages/react/src/components/Toggle/index.js – re-export the updated Toggle component so that the new prop is included in the public API.
• packages/react/src/components/Toggle/Toggle.stories.js – add readOnly to the argTypes & controls, include a default story demonstrating the readOnly state.
• packages/react/src/components/Toggle/Toggle-test.js – add RTL unit tests asserting that the Toggle has aria-readonly, the CSS class, and cannot be toggled via user events when readOnly=true.
• packages/react/src/components/ToggleSmall/index.js – mirror the readOnly prop support in the small variant, forwarding to the underlying input.
• packages/react/src/components/ToggleSmall/ToggleSmall-test.js – add RTL tests for the small Toggle’s readOnly behavior.
• packages/react/scss/components/toggle/_toggle.scss – define styling for the .bx--toggle--readonly modifier so readOnly toggles look enabled but non-interactive.
• e2e/components/Toggle/Toggle-test.e2e.js – add an end-to-end scenario that verifies in the browser that a readOnly Toggle is focusable (or not, per spec), announced correctly by a screenreader mock, and cannot be clicked to change state.
1.bug_scenario: The Toggle component currently doesn’t support a “readOnly” mode: you can’t set a Toggle to read-only (so that it’s announced as read-only by screen readers and cannot be changed) without also disabling it entirely (which styles it as “disabled” and prevents focus). The design mockups show a fully enabled-looking Toggle that is non-interactive but still announced as read-only. We need to add a readOnly prop (distinct from disabled), wire it through Toggle and ToggleSmall, style it with a new CSS modifier class, expose it in the story controls, and add RTL tests verifying that when readOnly is true (and disabled is false) the correct aria and CSS attributes are applied and the control can’t be toggled by user events.

2.explanation:
• Toggle.js (and ToggleSmall/index.js) need to accept a new `readOnly` prop, add the `bx--toggle--readonly` modifier class on the wrapper, and forward `readOnly` to the `<input>` so it can be skipped for pointer events but exposed to assistive technologies.  
• Toggle.test.js (and ToggleSmall.test.js) must include an RTL test asserting that when `readOnly` is passed, the rendered container has the correct modifier class and the underlying input has the `readOnly` attribute (but not `disabled`).  
• Toggle.stories.js needs to add the `readOnly` arg/control, configure a default story showcasing the `readOnly` state, and document the new prop for easy copy-and-paste.  
• _toggle.scss in carbon-components must define the styling for `.bx--toggle--readonly` (track, thumb, and label colors and spacing per the design), matching the enabled baseline but preventing pointer interaction.
2.bug_scenario: The current Toggle component only supports enabled/disabled states but doesn’t implement a true “read-only” mode. Per the reference designs, a read-only toggle should look like an enabled toggle (no greyed-out track), should not allow user clicks to change its state, but must remain exposed to screen readers so that “On/Off” is still announced. The provided artboards show the color (track and label), typography, spacing, and structure for small and big toggles in read-only mode (using a new `readonly` modifier).
